title: Submission / held-out scoring harness
context: The benchmark's evaluation integrity depends on a submission harness that scores predictions against held-out ground truth without leaking labels to participants. The harness must enforce the results schema (requiring split ID, seed(s), preprocessing hash, and compute provenance) and produce a structured result record for each evaluated submission. This prevents single-seed, unpinned, or undocumented claims from being submitted. The harness is a primary artifact of M2. See PLAN.md (Benchmark task + evaluation harness, Honest-reporting-by-construction results schema).
objective: Implement the submission and held-out scoring harness: accept a prediction file in the defined submission format, score it against the held-out test-set labels using the metric(s) from pathology-image-benchmarks-task-001, validate that the submission carries required metadata (split ID, seed(s), preprocessing hash, compute provenance), and produce a structured result record. The harness must not expose held-out labels to the submitter. Enforces the honest-reporting-by-construction results schema.
acceptanceCriteria: The harness accepts a prediction file in the defined submission format and scores it against held-out test labels using the metric(s) specified in pathology-image-benchmarks-task-001.
The harness validates that submissions carry required metadata: split ID, seed(s), preprocessing hash, and compute provenance; missing fields cause rejection, not silent scoring.
Held-out ground-truth labels are not exposed to the submitter at any point during the scoring process.
The harness produces a structured result record conforming to the results schema from pathology-image-benchmarks-prov-001.
The harness is implemented in the agent-neutral core (TypeScript/ESM) or as a documented Python adapter, consistent with the Hee-Lee Oss architecture rule.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; CI provenance gate passes on harness result records.
output: A submission and held-out scoring harness PR: prediction ingestion, metric computation, submission metadata validation, and structured result-record output, with passing CI gates.
